title: Scalable Community Detection Using Quantum Hamiltonian Descent and QUBO Formulation
problem: Community detection in large-scale graph data is computationally expensive with classical optimization; existing approaches lack scalability for diverse graph sizes and structures.
motivation: Efficient community detection is critical for analyzing complex networks and graph data; quantum-inspired methods offer potential speedup over classical approaches.
method: The approach reformulates community detection as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and applies Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) to find optimal community structures. A multi-level algorithm iteratively refines community assignments by alternating between QUBO setup and QHD-based optimization.
key_novelty: First hybrid quantum-inspired algorithm combining QHD with QUBO formulation for scalable community detection in large-scale graphs.
contributions: QUBO formulation of community detection problem amenable to quantum optimization
Multi-level iterative refinement algorithm using QHD
Demonstrates 5.49% better modularity scores with reduced computational time versus classical approaches
primary_theme: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent for scalable community detection
